title: Proverbs Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Proverbs chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Proverbs Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Proverbs Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Proverbs 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: My son, if thou be surety for thy friend
Go to the ant, thou sluggard
Deliver thyself as a roe from the hand of the hunter
Give not sleep to thine eyes
questions.correctAnswer: My son, if thou be surety for thy friend
questions.explanation: This is the very first verse of the chapter, as stated in Proverbs 6:1.

questions.question: What are you snared with, according to Proverbs 6?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:2 states that you are snared and taken with the words of your mouth.

questions.question: What should you do when you are in the hand of your friend?
options: Give not sleep to thine eyes
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:3 instructs to go, humble thyself, and make sure thy friend.

questions.question: What should you not give to your eyes?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:4 advises not to give sleep to thine eyes.

questions.question: How should you deliver yourself from danger?
options: As a bird from the hand of the fowler
As a man from his troubles
As a roe from the hand of the hunter
As a friend from a stranger
questions.correctAnswer: As a roe from the hand of the hunter
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:5 compares the urgency of delivering oneself to a roe escaping from a hunter.

questions.question: Who is advised to go to the ant?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:6 specifically addresses the sluggard to go to the ant.

questions.question: What does the ant not have according to Proverbs 6?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:7 states that the ant has no guide, overseer, or ruler.

questions.question: What does the ant provide in the summer?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:8 mentions that the ant provideth her meat in the summer.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 6:9 ask the sluggard?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:9 questions the sluggard about how long he will sleep.

questions.question: What does a little sleep lead to, according to Proverbs 6?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:11 states that poverty shall come as one that travelleth due to a little sleep.

questions.question: What characterizes a naughty person, according to Proverbs 6?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:12 indicates that a naughty person is a wicked man walking with a froward mouth.

questions.question: Is it true that you should not slumber to thine eyelids?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:4 instructs not to slumber to thine eyelids.

questions.question: Is it true that the ant gathers food in the harvest?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:8 states that the ant gathereth her food in the harvest.

questions.question: Is it false that the sluggard is advised to sleep more?
questions.explanation: The text does not advise the sluggard to sleep more; rather, it encourages him to wake up.

questions.question: Is it false that the ant has many rulers?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:7 states that the ant has no guide, overseer, or ruler.

medium.title: Proverbs Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Proverbs Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 6:13, which of the following behaviors is NOT mentioned as part of the deceitful man's actions?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:13 specifically mentions winking with eyes, speaking with feet, and teaching with fingers as deceitful behaviors, but it does not mention whispering with the mouth.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 6:15 promise will happen if someone continually devises mischief as stated in Proverbs 6:14?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:15 states that because the person devises mischief continually (Proverbs 6:14), his calamity will come suddenly and he will be broken without remedy.

questions.question: Which of the following is one of the seven things the LORD hates according to Proverbs 6:16-19?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:17 lists 'a lying tongue' as one of the six things the LORD hates and one of the seven abominations to Him.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 6:18-19, which two behaviors are included among those abominations to the LORD?
options: Feet that run swiftly to mischief and a false witness that speaketh lies
A cheerful heart and a willing spirit
Hands that heal and a tongue that encourages
Eyes that show mercy and feet that walk humbly
questions.correctAnswer: Feet that run swiftly to mischief and a false witness that speaketh lies
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:18-19 specify that 'feet that be swift in running to mischief' and 'a false witness that speaketh lies' are among the seven abominations to the LORD.

questions.question: What practical advice does Proverbs 6:20 give for living a wise and obedient life?
options: Keep thy father's commandment and forsake not the law of thy mother
Ignore the teachings of your parents
questions.correctAnswer: Keep thy father's commandment and forsake not the law of thy mother
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:20 instructs to keep the father's commandment and not forsake the mother's law as a foundation for wise living.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 6:21, how should one treat their parents’ commandments and laws?
options: Bind them continually upon thine heart and tie them about thy neck
questions.correctAnswer: Bind them continually upon thine heart and tie them about thy neck
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:21 advises to bind parental commandments continually on the heart and tie them about the neck, symbolizing constant remembrance and importance.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 6:22 say will happen when you keep your parents' commands bound upon your heart and neck?
options: It shall lead thee, keep thee when sleeping, and talk with thee when awake
It will make you wealthy instantly
It will cause you to be isolated
questions.correctAnswer: It shall lead thee, keep thee when sleeping, and talk with thee when awake
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:22 states that the commandments will guide, protect during sleep, and provide ongoing instruction.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 6:23 describe the commandment and the law?
options: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light
The commandment is a burden, and the law is darkness
The commandment is a chain, and the law is weight
The commandment is a door, and the law is a wall
questions.correctAnswer: The commandment is a lamp, and the law is light
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:23 uses the metaphor that the commandment is a lamp and the law is light, indicating guidance and illumination.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 6:24, what is one purpose of the commandments and laws?
options: To keep thee from the evil woman and from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman
To make life easier without effort
questions.correctAnswer: To keep thee from the evil woman and from the flattery of the tongue of a strange woman
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:24 explains that commandments serve to protect from temptation and harmful flattery.

questions.question: What warning is given in Proverbs 6:9-11 about laziness?
options: Poverty and want will come as a traveler and armed man
Slumber is a source of wisdom
questions.correctAnswer: Poverty and want will come as a traveler and armed man
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:11 warns that excessive sleep and slumber leads to poverty and want coming suddenly like a traveler or armed man.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 6:6-8 use the example of the ant to teach wisdom?
options: The ant works without overseer and gathers food in summer and harvest
The ant avoids work by following others
The ant asks for help from the fowler
questions.correctAnswer: The ant works without overseer and gathers food in summer and harvest
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:6-8 highlights the ant's diligence and self-motivation as an example of wise behavior.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 6:12 say about the character of a wicked person?
options: A naughty person, a wicked man, walks with a froward mouth
A wicked man is humble and kind
He speaks truth and seeks peace
questions.correctAnswer: A naughty person, a wicked man, walks with a froward mouth
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:12 describes the wicked person as someone who walks with a froward mouth, implying deceit and trouble.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 6:23 teaches that reproofs of instruction are the way of life.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:23 states that reproofs of instruction are the way of life, emphasizing the value of correction and teaching.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 6:17 says that a generous heart is one of the things the LORD hates.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:17 lists a proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood among the things the LORD hates; generosity is not mentioned.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 6:15 promises that the person who devises mischief will be rewarded with wealth and honor.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:15 states that the person who devises mischief will face sudden calamity and be broken without remedy, not rewarded.

hard.title: Proverbs Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Proverbs Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 6:25, what should one not lust after in their heart?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:25 explicitly states, 'Lust not after her beauty in thine heart;' instructing against desiring a woman's beauty internally.

questions.question: What consequence does Proverbs 6:26 associate with involvement with a 'whorish woman'?
options: A man is brought to a piece of bread
questions.correctAnswer: A man is brought to a piece of bread
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:26 says, 'For by means of a whorish woman a man is brought to a piece of bread,' indicating poverty or destitution results.

questions.question: In Proverbs 6:27, what analogy is used to illustrate the danger of indulging in sinful desires?
options: Taking fire in his bosom and his clothes not being burned
A bird caught in a snare
A ship caught in a storm
questions.correctAnswer: Taking fire in his bosom and his clothes not being burned
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:27 uses the analogy, 'Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burned?' to illustrate inevitable harm.

questions.question: According to Proverbs 6:29, what is said about a man who goes to his neighbour's wife?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:29 states, 'whosoever toucheth her shall not be innocent,' indicating guilt in adultery.

questions.question: What does Proverbs 6:31 say a thief must do if found stealing to satisfy hunger?
options: Restore sevenfold and give all the substance of his house
Pay a fine equal to the stolen goods
questions.correctAnswer: Restore sevenfold and give all the substance of his house
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:31 declares, 'he shall restore sevenfold; he shall give all the substance of his house,' emphasizing full restitution.

questions.question: What is the result of committing adultery according to Proverbs 6:32?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:32 warns, 'he that doeth it destroyeth his own soul,' highlighting severe spiritual consequences.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'nadah' in Proverbs 6:23 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'nadah' used in Proverbs 6:23 means 'commandment,' referring to divine instruction.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Proverbs 6:27-28 with the fire and hot coals imagery?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:27-28 employs rhetorical questions to emphasize the inevitability of harm from sin, a persuasive literary technique.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the warning against lust found in Proverbs 6:25?
questions.explanation: Matthew 5:28 echoes Proverbs 6:25 by teaching that looking at a woman lustfully is committing adultery in the heart.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage corresponds to the theme of restoration after theft mentioned in Proverbs 6:31?
questions.explanation: Exodus 22:1 aligns with Proverbs 6:31 by prescribing restitution for theft, reinforcing the biblical principle of making full amends.

questions.question: What verse directly precedes Proverbs 6:25 in the chapter?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:24 precedes 6:25 and speaks about keeping one from the evil woman, setting the context for the admonition in 6:25.

questions.question: What is the primary theme of Proverbs 6:16-19, preceding the final section of Proverbs 6?
options: The importance of the ant’s wisdom
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:16-19 lists six things the LORD hates and seven abominations, highlighting sinful behaviors God detests.

questions.question: From a cultural-historical perspective, what does 'sevenfold restitution' in Proverbs 6:31 indicate about ancient Israelite justice?
options: It emphasizes thorough compensation for wrongdoing
It was a symbolic number with no legal weight
It meant the thief was forgiven without payment
It referred to seven years of servitude
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes thorough compensation for wrongdoing
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:31 reflects the ancient Israelite principle of making full and generous restitution, as seen also in Exodus 22:1.

questions.question: Which literary structure can be observed in Proverbs 6:16-19 listing the 'six things' and 'seven abominations'?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:16-19 uses numerical parallelism, a common Hebrew poetic device, to emphasize completeness of what is detested.

questions.question: True or False: Proverbs 6:34-35 suggests that jealousy will accept ransom or gifts to stop vengeance.
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:34-35 states jealousy will not regard any ransom nor be content with many gifts, indicating vengeance cannot be bought off.

theological.title: Proverbs Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Proverbs Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 6:16 teach about God's nature in relation to moral evil?
options: God hates certain sins as abominations
God is indifferent to human sin
questions.correctAnswer: God hates certain sins as abominations
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:16 states 'These six things doth the LORD hate: yea, seven are an abomination unto him,' demonstrating God's hatred for specific sins, indicating His holiness and moral purity.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sinfulness is taught in Proverbs 6:12-14?
options: Sin manifests in deceitful and disruptive behavior
Sin is primarily ignorance without malice
Sin only affects external actions, not the heart
Sin is always obvious and publicly known
questions.correctAnswer: Sin manifests in deceitful and disruptive behavior
questions.explanation: Verses 12-14 describe a wicked person who uses deceitful gestures and words to sow discord, showing that sin operates through subtle and harmful social actions.

questions.question: What doctrine does Proverbs 6:20-23 teach about the role of parental instruction in sanctification?
options: Parental commands and law guide and protect believers
Parental advice is optional and not spiritually necessary
Sanctification is only through mystical experience
questions.correctAnswer: Parental commands and law guide and protect believers
questions.explanation: Verses 20-23 emphasize binding parental commandments on the heart and neck as a lamp and light, signifying the essential role of God's law and parental instruction in sanctification.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 6:17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:17 lists sins that God hates, showing His holiness and moral perfection that cannot tolerate sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by the counsel to 'go to the ant' in Proverbs 6:6?
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:6 uses the ant's industriousness as an example of wisdom in human conduct, reflecting God's impartation of wisdom for right living.

questions.question: How does Proverbs 6:25-26 connect to the broader biblical theme of human temptation and divine warning?
options: It warns that yielding to lust leads to destruction
It encourages indulgence in beauty without restraint
It denies any consequences for sinful desires
It teaches that temptation is not a serious issue
questions.correctAnswer: It warns that yielding to lust leads to destruction
questions.explanation: Verses 25-26 warn against lusting after a strange woman, illustrating the theme that temptation leads to spiritual and physical ruin, consistent with biblical warnings elsewhere.

questions.question: In what way does Proverbs 6:30-31 prepare for New Testament teachings on restitution and justice?
options: It teaches that thieves must restore more than they took
It permits theft without consequence when hungry
It advocates ignoring justice for the poor
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that thieves must restore more than they took
questions.explanation: Verses 30-31 state that a thief must restore sevenfold, prefiguring New Testament teachings on justice and restitution (e.g., Luke 19:8).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 6:4 and 6:5 teach about human responsibility and deliverance?
options: Humility and urgent self-deliverance are necessary for escape
Deliverance is assured regardless of action
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and urgent self-deliverance are necessary for escape
questions.explanation: Verse 4 commands not to give sleep to eyes, and verse 5 urges delivering oneself like a roe from the hunter, teaching the doctrine of active humility and responsibility in deliverance.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 6:16-19 and Proverbs 6:12-14 teach about the nature and consequences of sin?
options: Sin is both an internal disposition and external disruptive action leading to sudden calamity
Sin is merely external and harmless
Sin is always forgiven without consequence
Sin is only a minor moral failing
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is both an internal disposition and external disruptive action leading to sudden calamity
questions.explanation: Verses 12-14 describe sinful behavior, while 16-19 list sins God hates, establishing that sin involves corrupt heart intentions and disruptive actions with inevitable judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Proverbs 6:20-23 and Proverbs 6:24-25 teach regarding the role of God's law in moral purity?
options: God's law is a guiding light that protects from sexual immorality
God's law is irrelevant to purity
questions.correctAnswer: God's law is a guiding light that protects from sexual immorality
questions.explanation: Verses 20-23 describe the law as a lamp and light guiding the believer, and verses 24-25 warn against lusting, showing the law's protective role in sanctification.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Proverbs 6:30-31 is unjust because it demands excessive restitution from a thief. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Restitution must be generous to uphold justice and deter sin
The thief is excused if hungry
The passage encourages leniency for the poor
questions.correctAnswer: Restitution must be generous to uphold justice and deter sin
questions.explanation: Proverbs 6:30-31 mandates restoring sevenfold, teaching that justice requires not only making amends but also deterring future wrongdoing.

questions.question: What doctrine about human accountability is taught in Proverbs 6:1-3 regarding suretyship?
options: One must humbly seek to avoid financial entanglements
One is free from consequences after suretyship
Suretyship is irrelevant to covenant faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: One must humbly seek to avoid financial entanglements
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 warn against rash suretyship and urge humble action to deliver oneself, teaching accountability and prudence in commitments.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Proverbs 6:15 illustrate through the sudden calamity upon the wicked?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states the wicked will be broken suddenly without remedy, showing God's attribute of executing righteous justice swiftly.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Proverbs 6:34-35 have with New Testament teachings on jealousy and vengeance?
options: It anticipates the destructive nature of jealousy, contrasting with Christ's call to love and forgiveness
It endorses personal vengeance as godly
It denies the problem of jealousy
It teaches jealousy as a virtue
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the destructive nature of jealousy, contrasting with Christ's call to love and forgiveness
questions.explanation: Verses 34-35 describe jealousy as rage leading to uncompromising vengeance, which New Testament teachings (e.g., Romans 12:19) counter by advocating forgiveness.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sloth and divine warning is taught in Proverbs 6:9-11?
options: Sloth leads to sudden poverty and want
Sloth is harmless and without consequence
Sloth is recommended for spiritual growth
questions.correctAnswer: Sloth leads to sudden poverty and want
questions.explanation: Verses 9-11 warn that continued sleep and slumber cause poverty to come as a traveler and want as an armed man, teaching the consequences of laziness.
